spec: The entry function `schedule(hangars)` receives a tuple of eight lists of aircraft model strings for Boeing, Airbus, Embraer, Bombardier, Cessna, Gulfstream, Piper, and Beechcraft. It returns a tuple of eight maintenance reports. For Boeing, append the service bay index to each model string. For Airbus, find the bay index of the first string equaling A380. For Embraer, create a dictionary mapping the bay index to the model string. For Bombardier, filter out models located at odd bay indices. For Cessna, format a checklist string combining the bay index and the model. For Gulfstream, return a list of tuples pairing the bay index with the model string. For Piper, find the bay index of the model with the most characters. For Beechcraft, create a dictionary linking the bay index to the string mechanic assigned. Example: given an Airbus list of A320 then A380, the result is the index one.

title: Marketing Engagement Tracker
spec: The entry function `track(platforms)` takes a tuple of eight lists of integer click counts for Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, and Snapchat. It returns a tuple of eight engagement metrics. For Facebook, multiply each click count by its day index. For Twitter, find the day index of the first day with exactly zero clicks. For Instagram, create a dictionary mapping the day index to the click count. For LinkedIn, filter out counts located at day indices greater than twenty. For TikTok, format a weekly report string combining the day index and the click count. For YouTube, return a list of tuples pairing the day index with the view count. For Pinterest, find the day index of the highest click count. For Snapchat, calculate the sum of the clicks on days with even day indices.

title: Compiler Syntax Highlighter
spec: The entry function `highlight(tokens)` receives a tuple of eight lists of code token strings categorized as keywords, identifiers, literals, operators, comments, punctuators, whitespace, and directives. It returns a tuple of eight formatting instructions. For keywords, append a color code string derived from the sequence index. For identifiers, find the sequence index of the first token starting with an underscore. For literals, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to the token character length. For operators, filter out tokens located at sequence indices less than five. For comments, format an HTML span string that includes the sequence index and the token. For punctuators, return a list of tuples of the sequence index and the token string. For whitespace, find the sequence index of the longest whitespace string. For directives, create a dictionary linking the sequence index to the directive name string.

title: Cipher Sequence Mixer
spec: The entry function `mix(sequences)` takes a tuple of eight lists of integers labeled alpha, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon, zeta, eta, and theta. It returns a tuple of eight cryptographic transformations. For alpha, add the position index to each integer. For beta, find the position index of the first negative integer. For gamma, create a dictionary mapping the position index to the integer squared. For delta, filter out integers located at position indices divisible by five. For epsilon, format a hexadecimal string combining the position index and the integer. For zeta, return a list of tuples pairing the position index with the integer. For eta, find the position index of the maximum integer. For theta, calculate the sum of the integers located at odd position indices. Example: a beta list of five and negative two yields a position index of one.

title: Wildlife Sanctuary Feeder
spec: The entry function `feed(enclosures)` accepts a tuple of eight lists of animal species strings for primates, felines, canines, ursids, herbivores, reptiles, avians, and amphibians. It returns a tuple of eight feeding schedules. For primates, append the feeding sequence index to each species string. For felines, find the sequence index of the first string equaling tiger. For canines, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to the species. For ursids, filter out species located at even sequence indices. For herbivores, format a diet chart string combining the sequence index and the species. For reptiles, return a list of tuples pairing the sequence index with the species string. For avians, find the sequence index of the shortest species name. For amphibians, create a dictionary of the sequence index to a habitat temperature integer.

title: Solar Array Calibrator
spec: The entry function `calibrate(panels)` receives a tuple of eight lists of float voltage readings for arrays A through H. It returns a tuple of eight calibration outputs. For array A, add the sequence index multiplied by a small calibration factor to each reading. For array B, find the sequence index of the first reading below twelve volts. For array C, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to the expected output float. For array D, filter out readings located at sequence indices greater than fifteen. For array E, format a log entry string combining the sequence index and the voltage. For array F, return a list of tuples of the sequence index and the reading. For array G, find the sequence index of the maximum reading. For array H, calculate the sum of the voltages located at odd sequence indices.

title: Manuscript Preservation Scraper
spec: The entry function `scrape(collections)` takes a tuple of eight lists of document title strings for letters, diaries, maps, photographs, blueprints, receipts, newspapers, and journals. It returns a tuple of eight archival indices. For letters, append the scan sequence index to each title. For diaries, find the sequence index of the first untitled document string. For maps, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to a resolution integer. For photographs, filter out titles located at odd sequence indices. For blueprints, format a metadata string combining the sequence index and the title. For receipts, return a list of tuples pairing the sequence index with the title string. For newspapers, find the sequence index of the longest title. For journals, create a dictionary of the sequence index to the author name string.

title: Quantum Computer Simulator
spec: The entry function `simulate(registers)` accepts a tuple of eight lists of float probabilities representing qubits in registers one through eight. It returns a tuple of eight quantum state evaluations. For register one, multiply each probability by its sequence index. For register two, find the sequence index of the first probability over zero point five. For register three, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to a computed phase angle float. For register four, filter out probabilities located at sequence indices divisible by three. For register five, format a state vector string combining the sequence index and the probability. For register six, return a list of tuples pairing the sequence index with the probability. For register seven, find the sequence index of the minimum probability. For register eight, calculate the sum of the probabilities located at even sequence indices.

title: Election Results Tabulator
spec: The entry function `tabulate(precincts)` receives a tuple of eight lists of integer vote counts for North, South, East, West, Central, Coastal, Valley, and Mountain regions. It returns a tuple of eight certified totals. For North, add the sequence index to each count to account for absentee ballots. For South, find the sequence index of the first count exceeding ten thousand. For East, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to the vote count. For West, filter out counts located at odd sequence indices. For Central, format an official record string combining the sequence index and the count. For Coastal, return a list of tuples of the sequence index and the count. For Valley, find the sequence index of the highest count. For Mountain, calculate the sum of the counts located at prime-like sequence indices consisting of two, three, five, and seven.

title: Terrain Mapping Extractor
spec: The entry function `extract(bands)` takes a tuple of eight lists of integer pixel intensities for red, green, blue, near infrared, shortwave infrared, thermal, panchromatic, and microwave bands. It returns a tuple of eight image processing results. For the red band, multiply each intensity by its sequence index. For the green band, find the sequence index of the first pure white pixel represented by two hundred fifty five. For the blue band, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to the intensity. For the near infrared band, filter out pixels located at sequence indices less than one hundred. For the shortwave infrared band, format a hexadecimal string combining the sequence index and the intensity. For the thermal band, return a list of tuples pairing the sequence index with the intensity. For the panchromatic band, find the sequence index of the darkest pixel. For the microwave band, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to the intensity.

title: Commodity Trend Evaluator
spec: The entry function `evaluate(commodities)` accepts a tuple of eight lists of daily integer closing prices for gold, silver, oil, natural gas, wheat, corn, soybeans, and coffee. It returns a tuple of eight market analyses. For gold, add the day sequence index to each price. For silver, find the sequence index of the first price dropping below twenty. For oil, create a dictionary mapping the sequence index to the price. For natural gas, filter out prices located at even sequence indices. For wheat, format a ticker string combining the sequence index and the price. For corn, return a list of tuples pairing the sequence index with the price. For soybeans, find the sequence index of the highest price. For coffee, calculate the sum of the prices on days with odd sequence indices. Example: given an oil list of fifty and sixty, it returns a dictionary mapping zero to fifty and one to sixty.

title: Tournament Match Scorer
spec: A module to evaluate a sports match from a list of play strings. The entry point is `score(plays)`. It must parse the strings to identify scoring events, using the position in the sequence to determine the chronological play ID. The logic must evaluate team fouls by isolating penalty events, applying a bonus multiplier derived from the foul's sequence number within the match. It needs to generate a formatted chronological log where each entry starts with its overall event number. Additionally, it must rank the scoring events by value and output a highlight reel where each line is prefixed with its placement number. It should calculate a momentum metric by weighting each play's score by its chronological index. Finally, the system must compile a numbered list of defensive blocks and output a final statistical summary with sequentially numbered sections. Example input: a list of play description strings. Output: a detailed match report tuple.

title: Image Watermark Extractor
spec: A module to pull a hidden text message from a list of integer pixel values. The entry point is `extract(pixels)`. It must process the pixels to extract the least significant bit, recording the pixel's coordinate number to log where corrupted bits occur. The extracted bits must be grouped into bytes, using the bit's position in the group to calculate its binary weight. The system should validate the byte sequence by applying a parity check that multiplies each byte value by its position index in the sequence. It needs to format a hexadecimal dump of the decoded bytes, with each line starting with the absolute memory offset. The logic must also identify marker sequences by comparing each byte's position to known header offsets. Finally, it should generate a comprehensive report of the extraction process, numbering each diagnostic message for easy reference. Example input: a list of integers. Output: the decoded string and a list of numbered log lines.

title: Freight Train Dispatcher
spec: A module to organize a freight train given a sequence of cargo weights. The entry point is `dispatch(carriages)`. It must validate the train composition by ensuring heavy cars are properly spaced, using the carriage position to verify placement. The logic calculates the total moment of inertia by multiplying each carriage's weight by its distance from the front, represented by its position sequence. It needs to identify hazardous materials and log their exact position number in the train for safety inspectors. The system must allocate crew members to observation cars, assigning them based on the car's order in the sequence. It should format a complete train manifest where every printed line begins with the carriage number. Additionally, it must group the carriages into destination blocks, numbering each block sequentially, and generate a final numbered list of dispatch instructions for the yardmaster. Example input: a list of weights. Output: a formatted dispatch report.

title: Mail Delivery Router
spec: A module to optimize a postal delivery sequence. The entry point is `route(addresses)`. It must process a list of delivery stops, assigning each a sequential stop ID based on its order. The logic calculates an estimated arrival time by adding a fixed duration multiplied by the stop's position in the route. It needs to flag any heavy packages, recording their sequence number to alert the loader. The system must generate a formatted itinerary where every destination is numbered starting from one. It should calculate a fuel usage metric that increases progressively by multiplying the package weight by its delivery sequence order. Finally, it must log any address validation errors by referencing the exact line number of the failed address, and output a numbered summary of driver break times scheduled between specific stops. Example input: a list of address strings. Output: a routing summary and itinerary lines.

title: Skyscraper Lift Controller
spec: A module to manage elevator operations from a sequence of requested floor numbers. The entry point is `operate(requests)`. It must process the requests, assigning a chronological ticket number to each passenger based on their order of arrival. The logic computes the total waiting penalty by multiplying the requested floor by its position in the queue. It needs to identify invalid floor requests and log an error message containing the exact request number. The system must generate a passenger manifest where each assigned cabin is printed with its sequence number. It should also calculate mechanical wear by scaling the travel distance by the operation's chronological index. Finally, it must format an end-of-day travel log, numbering each trip sequentially, and output a summarized list of maintenance alerts prioritized by their occurrence order. Example input: a list of integers. Output: an operation log and maintenance summary.

title: Family Lineage Tracer
spec: A module to analyze a family tree provided as a list of generational group sizes. The entry point is `trace(generations)`. It must process each generation, using its depth index to calculate a genetic dilution factor for inherited traits. The logic should assign a Roman numeral identifier to each generation based on its sequence position. It needs to identify generations with unusually low birth rates, logging the exact generation number for historical review. The system must format a genealogical report where each line is indented by a space multiplier equal to the generation depth. It should also calculate a compound wealth distribution metric by multiplying a base asset value by the generation's chronological index. Finally, it must generate a numbered list of notable ancestors and output a step-by-step lineage breakdown where each step is explicitly numbered. Example input: a list of population counts. Output: a formatted lineage text.

title: Assembly Execution Simulator
spec: A module to trace the execution of machine code given a list of instruction strings. The entry point is `execute(instructions)`. It must parse the instructions, treating the sequence position as the memory address for the program counter. The logic calculates jump offsets by comparing target addresses with the current instruction's position index. It needs to identify privileged operations and log a security warning that includes the exact line number of the instruction. The system must generate an execution trace log where every output line is prefixed with its step number. It should simulate a pipeline delay by applying a wait cycle penalty that scales with the instruction's chronological index. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of accessed registers and output a formatted memory dump where each block is sequentially numbered. Example input: a list of command strings. Output: an execution trace and memory state.

title: Embroidery Stitch Planner
spec: A module to guide an automated sewing machine using a list of stitch types. The entry point is `plan(stitches)`. It must process the sequence, assigning a coordinate step number to each stitch based on its order. The logic calculates thread consumption by multiplying the stitch length by a tension factor derived from its position sequence. It needs to identify color change commands and log the exact stitch number where the operator must intervene. The system must generate a printed pattern guide where every instruction line begins with a sequential ID. It should calculate fabric stress metrics by weighting each dense stitch by its chronological position. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of required thread spools and output a step-by-step machine calibration sequence, with each step clearly numbered. Example input: a list of stitch commands. Output: a sewing plan and calibration steps.

title: Submarine Telegraph Decoder
spec: A module to translate underwater acoustic transmissions given a list of duration values. The entry point is `decode(signals)`. It must evaluate each signal duration, assigning a chronological time slot number based on its sequence order. The logic differentiates between dots and dashes, calculating a signal degradation metric by multiplying the duration by its position in the message. It needs to detect interference spikes and log an anomaly report containing the exact sequence number of the corrupted signal. The system must generate a formatted transcript where each decoded word is numbered for verification. It should compute a transmission checksum by summing the signal values weighted by their position indices. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of origin coordinates and output a final communication log with sequentially numbered entries. Example input: a list of float durations. Output: a transcript and diagnostic logs.

title: Hard Drive Organizer
spec: A module to optimize storage space given a list of file segment identifiers. The entry point is `defragment(sectors)`. It must evaluate each sector, treating its sequence position as the absolute physical address on the disk platter. The logic calculates the seek time penalty by multiplying the segment size by its physical block index. It needs to identify bad sectors and log a hardware warning that includes the exact address number. The system must generate a data movement plan where every relocation instruction is sequentially numbered. It should calculate a fragmentation score by comparing each segment's value to its position sequence. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of consolidated free spaces and output a formatted disk map where each visual row is prefixed with its block number. Example input: a list of string identifiers. Output: a movement plan and disk map.

title: Printing Press Formatter
spec: A module to prepare text for physical printing given a sequence of paragraph strings. The entry point is `typeset(paragraphs)`. It must process the text blocks, assigning a sequential block ID to each paragraph based on its order. The logic calculates the vertical page offset by multiplying the line height by the paragraph's sequence position. It needs to detect oversized words that break margins and log a layout error detailing the exact paragraph number. The system must generate a final print preview where every page line is explicitly numbered. It should apply a fading ink simulation by decreasing the color density based on the paragraph's chronological index. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of required metal typefaces and output a formatted table of contents with sequentially numbered sections. Example input: a list of text paragraphs. Output: a formatted document and error log.

title: Choreography Formation Planner
spec: A module to design a stage performance from a list of dancer position strings. The entry point is `choreograph(moves)`. It must evaluate each movement, assigning a chronological beat number based on its sequence order in the routine. The logic calculates the total stage distance covered by multiplying the step width by the move's position index. It needs to identify dangerous collisions and log a safety warning that includes the exact beat number of the hazard. The system must generate a script for the lighting crew where every cue is sequentially numbered. It should compute an exhaustion metric by scaling the movement intensity by its chronological position in the performance. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of prop changes and output a formatted stage map where each formation is explicitly numbered. Example input: a list of move descriptors. Output: a choreography script and stage metrics.

title: Tactile Graphics Renderer
spec: A module to generate Braille documents from a sequence of depth values. The entry point is `emboss(points)`. It must process the points, treating the sequence position as the linear coordinate on the embossing paper. The logic calculates the required mechanical pressure by multiplying the depth value by its position index to account for roller wear. It needs to identify invalid depth readings and log a hardware calibration error containing the exact point number. The system must generate a machine command file where every punch instruction is sequentially numbered. It should compute a tactile contrast score by weighting each raised dot by its chronological position. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of page breaks and output a formatted preview grid where each row is prefixed with its line number. Example input: a list of integer depths. Output: a list of commands and a preview.

title: Kiosk Inventory Manager
spec: A module to oversee automated vending machines given a list of product quantities. The entry point is `restock(slots)`. It must evaluate each dispenser spiral, assigning a physical slot ID based on its sequence order. The logic calculates the restocking cost by multiplying the item price by an access difficulty multiplier derived from the slot's position. It needs to identify expired perishable goods and log a disposal order that includes the exact slot number. The system must generate a warehouse picking list where every requested item is sequentially numbered. It should compute an electricity usage estimate by weighting the refrigeration need by the slot's physical index. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of required coin refills and output a formatted inventory report with numbered rows. Example input: a list of product counts. Output: a restocking list and management report.

title: Darts Match Referee
spec: A module to oversee a pub game from a sequence of point values. The entry point is `referee(throws)`. It must evaluate each dart thrown, assigning a chronological throw number based on its sequence order. The logic calculates the running score by applying a fatigue penalty that multiplies the point value by its position index in the round. It needs to identify foul line violations and log a penalty record detailing the exact throw number. The system must generate a live scoreboard feed where every recorded hit is sequentially numbered. It should compute a precision metric by weighting treble hits by their chronological order in the match. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of suggested checkout combinations and output a formatted match summary with sequentially numbered legs. Example input: a list of point integers. Output: a scoreboard log and match summary.

title: Binary Firmware Extractor
spec: A module to analyze raw device code from a list of integer byte values. The entry point is `dump(bytes)`. It must evaluate the data, treating the sequence position as the absolute memory address offset. The logic calculates a cumulative checksum by multiplying each byte value by its memory address index. It needs to detect corrupted magic numbers and log an integrity failure containing the exact byte offset. The system must generate a hexadecimal memory dump where every printed row begins with its address number. It should apply a decryption cipher that shifts the byte value by an amount equal to its chronological position. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of extracted string literals and output a formatted extraction log where each step is sequentially numbered. Example input: a list of integer bytes. Output: a memory dump and extraction log.

title: Industrial Furnace Profiler
spec: A module to monitor a factory kiln using a sequence of thermal readings. The entry point is `profile(temperatures)`. It must process the data, assigning a chronological minute timestamp to each reading based on its sequence order. The logic calculates the thermal stress on the ceramic lining by multiplying the temperature by its time index. It needs to identify dangerous heat spikes and log a critical alarm that includes the exact minute number. The system must generate a cooling schedule where every ramp-down instruction is sequentially numbered. It should compute an energy consumption metric by weighting the heater output by its chronological position in the cycle. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of sensor calibration checks and output a formatted firing report with sequentially numbered phases. Example input: a list of temperature floats. Output: a cooling schedule and firing report.

title: Aquarium Tank Manager
spec: A module to maintain a commercial fish habitat from a list of water quality readings. The entry point is `manage(parameters)`. It must evaluate each measurement, assigning a chronological hour ID based on its sequence order. The logic calculates the chemical dosing requirement by multiplying the toxicity level by its time index to account for accumulation. It needs to identify critical oxygen drops and log an emergency aeration alert detailing the exact hour number. The system must generate a feeding schedule where every dispersed meal is sequentially numbered. It should compute a filter degradation metric by weighting the particulate count by its chronological position in the day. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of required manual cleanings and output a formatted daily log with sequentially numbered entries. Example input: a list of float measurements. Output: a maintenance schedule and daily log.

title: Billiards Tournament Tracker
spec: A module to record a pool match given a sequence of pocketed ball numbers. The entry point is `track(shots)`. It must evaluate each successful shot, assigning a chronological inning number based on its sequence order. The logic calculates the total prize money multiplier by multiplying the ball number by its position index in the run. It needs to identify table scratches and log a foul penalty that includes the exact shot number. The system must generate a spectator display feed where every recorded strike is sequentially numbered. It should compute a player momentum score by weighting consecutive pots by their chronological order. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of defensive safety plays and output a formatted match bracket with sequentially numbered rounds. Example input: a list of ball integers. Output: a spectator feed and tournament bracket.

title: Ski Resort Avalanche Monitor
spec: A module to ensure mountain safety from a list of snow accumulation measurements. The entry point is `monitor(depths)`. It must evaluate the sensor data, assigning an elevation zone ID to each reading based on its sequence order. The logic calculates the structural instability risk by multiplying the snow depth by an incline factor derived from its position index. It needs to identify sudden frozen layers and log a detonation warning detailing the exact zone number. The system must generate a ski patrol route plan where every inspection checkpoint is sequentially numbered. It should compute a wind loading metric by weighting the accumulation by its chronological position in the storm cycle. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of closed trails and output a formatted public broadcast with sequentially numbered safety advisories. Example input: a list of float depths. Output: a route plan and safety broadcast.

title: Cinema Booking System
spec: A module to allocate theater seating from a sequence of group sizes. The entry point is `book(requests)`. It must process the incoming groups, assigning a chronological reservation ID based on their order in the sequence. The logic calculates the total ticket cost by adding a prime seating surcharge multiplied by the group's position index in the queue. It needs to identify invalid negative requests and log a rejection notice containing the exact reservation number. The system must generate a printable ticket roll where every issued pass is sequentially numbered. It should compute a concession stand demand forecast by weighting the group size by its chronological arrival index. Finally, it must compile a numbered list of seating upgrades and output a formatted daily seating manifest with sequentially numbered rows. Example input: a list of integer group sizes. Output: a ticket roll and seating manifest.

title: Concert Rigging Inspector

spec: Build a multi stage processing pipeline using separate functions. The entry function `sequence(beats)` accepts a list of volume levels from zero to nine. First, identify downbeats which are elements located at even positions with maximum volume. Second, create a syncopation list by finding positions where the volume is higher than the immediate next element. Third, apply a fade out effect by subtracting the position index from the volume for the second half of the sequence. Finally, generate a track log numbering each beat starting from zero alongside its final adjusted volume. Return the total volume and the track logs.

title: Morse Code Signal Decoder
spec: Divide the logic into multiple decoding steps. The entry function `decode(durations)` receives a list of integers representing milliseconds. Separate the list into marks and spaces based on whether their sequence position is even or odd. For marks, classify as a dot or dash and record their original sequence index. For spaces, use their duration to identify character gaps and record their index. Reconstruct letters by grouping marks between gaps, and generate a transmission report that prefixes every decoded character with its original mark index. Return the decoded string and the transmission report.

title: Bookshelf Organization Planner
spec: Use helper functions to manage shelf allocation. The entry function `organize(books)` takes a list of book thickness integers. Divide the books into shelves where each holds up to fifty units of thickness, tracking the original sequence index of each book. Identify heavy books thicker than ten and place a bookend after them if the next book in the original list is thin. Create a shelf manifest that lists the shelf number and the books it contains by their sequence index. Find the widest book on each shelf and note its position on that shelf. Return the manifests and the total number of bookends needed.

title: Airport Luggage Carousel Router
spec: Implement a multi step routing system. The entry function `route(bags)` takes a list of weight integers for checked bags. Filter out oversized bags weighing more than fifty, recording their sequence arrival number. Distribute the remaining bags across three loading carts in a round robin fashion based on their arrival order. Calculate a balance score for each cart by comparing each assigned bag to the previous bag on that same cart. Generate a routing manifest where each entry contains the chronological arrival number and the assigned cart. Return the manifests and the oversized bag positions.

title: Barter Trade Chain Validator
spec: Structure the validation into distinct phases. The entry function `validate(trades)` receives a list of integer values representing traded goods. Verify that each trade value is within twenty percent of the previous trade value in the sequence. Flag any position where the value drops by more than half compared to the very first trade. Extract all trades that form a local maximum compared to their immediate neighbors in the sequence. Produce an audit trail string for every trade stating its step number and value. Return the audit trail, the count of valid steps, and the flagged positions.

title: Plinko Board Path Simulator
spec: Build a simulation pipeline. The entry function `simulate(drops)` accepts a list of directional shifts, negative for left and positive for right. Track the horizontal position of the puck at each step starting from zero. Record the sequence index whenever the puck hits a boundary at position negative five or positive five. Calculate the momentum by multiplying the current shift by its drop step number. Generate a path log detailing the step index and the resulting horizontal position. Find the longest consecutive fall in the same direction and its starting step index. Return the path log and the boundary hit indices.

title: Axe Throwing Tournament Scorer
spec: Use helper functions to evaluate the match. The entry function `score(throws)` receives a list of integer ring scores from zero to five. Divide the throws into rounds of three. For each round, calculate the sum and apply a clutch bonus if the third throw in that round is a five. Track the overall throw number across the entire game. Identify consecutive bullseyes where a five is followed immediately by another five in the sequence. Generate a match report string for each throw stating its overall position number and the score. Return the total score and the match report.

title: Lockpicking Tumbler Sequence Simulator
spec: Model the lockpicking process using separate step functions. The entry function `simulate(tumblers)` accepts a list of integers representing required pin heights. Simulate a tool lifting each pin sequentially, where a pin requiring a height greater than seven adds a penalty to the effective height of all subsequent pins. Record the sequence position of any pin that perfectly matches the base tool height. Generate an unlock sequence log that numbers each pin from one and shows its adjusted height. Determine if any two adjacent pins have an adjusted height difference greater than five. Return the sequence log and the perfect pin positions.

title: Mechanical Typewriter Ribbon Simulator
spec: Structure the simulation with multiple helpers. The entry function `typewrite(strokes)` receives a list of integer impact forces. Simulate ink depletion where each stroke reduces the ribbon ink level based on its position in the sequence. Identify ghost characters where the impact force is high but the ink level has dropped below ten, recording their chronological stroke number. Apply a ribbon reverse operation every fifty strokes. Produce a printed page log showing the stroke number and the effective darkness of the character. Return the printed page log and the ghost character positions.

title: Abacus Bead Movement Calculator
spec: Break down the calculation into multiple phases. The entry function `calculate(movements)` takes a list of integer values representing numbers to add. Split each number into column values for units, tens, and hundreds. Keep a running tally and for each addition, record the operation number and the number of beads moved in the tens column. Identify any step position where a carry operation cascades across all three columns. Create a calculation receipt that pairs the step number with the current running total. Return the final sum, the receipt, and the positions with cascading carries.

title: Braille Character Translator
spec: Use helper functions to decode the sequence. The entry function `translate(dots)` receives a list of integers where each represents a six bit braille dot pattern. Convert each integer to a letter using a standard mapping. Detect capitalization markers and apply uppercase to the subsequent letter based on its sequence position. Identify numbers by looking for the number marker and converting the next sequence of characters to digits until a space is encountered. Create a transcription log where each line contains the original sequence index and the translated character. Return the final string and the transcription log.

title: Photocopier Collator Manager
spec: Organize the collation process into distinct steps. The entry function `collate(pages)` accepts a list of integers representing page numbers in a raw scan. Group the pages into individual document sets by splitting the sequence whenever a page number is lower than the previous one. Identify blank pages which are represented by zero and record their absolute position in the feed. Generate a collator tray manifest detailing the feed sequence number and the assigned document set for each page. Find the largest document set and its starting sequence index. Return the document sets and the manifest.

title: Book Index Page Compiler
spec: Structure the compilation using helper functions. The entry function `compile(terms)` receives a list of strings representing extracted keywords in reading order. Group the terms alphabetically while keeping track of the chronological appearance number for each term. Identify duplicate terms that appear within five positions of each other and discard the later ones. Format the index by pairing each unique term with its first appearance number. Create a cross reference log that states the appearance number and the term for every discarded duplicate. Return the formatted index and the cross reference log.

title: Laser Tag Arena Zone Controller
spec: Implement the zone management logic in phases. The entry function `manage(zones)` takes a list of integers representing player counts in different arena sectors. Monitor the density of each sector, activating a dispersal warning for any sector with more than ten players and applying it to the immediate next sector as well. Calculate a sector utilization score by multiplying the player count by the sector sequence number. Find the sector with the largest player drop off compared to the previous sector. Generate a zone status report linking the sector number to its warning state. Return the total player count and the status report.

title: Demolition Blast Sequencer
spec: Use multiple functions to plan the staggered detonation. The entry function `sequence(blasts)` accepts a list of integer explosive charges in pounds. Calculate the delay for each charge, where each must detonate a specific number of milliseconds after the previous one based on its position in the chain. Identify primary charges weighing over fifty pounds and double the delay for the subsequent charge. Generate a firing schedule that pairs the detonation sequence number with the absolute time in milliseconds. Track the position of any charge that is significantly smaller than the one before it. Return the firing schedule and the flagged positions.

title: Fencing Match Touch Scorer
spec: Divide the scoring logic into helpers. The entry function `score(touches)` receives a list of strings representing valid target hits by left or right fencer. Award points to the corresponding fencer, tracking the chronological bout number for every touch. If the right fencer scores three touches in a row, award a momentum point on the third touch based on its position. Identify double touches if the sequence contains left and right hits in alternating succession for four turns. Generate a bout log that strings together the bout number and the current score tally. Return the final score and the bout log.

title: Vending Machine Inventory Restocker
spec: Structure the restocking calculations into separate steps. The entry function `restock(items)` takes a list of integers representing current stock levels for snack spirals. Determine which spirals need refilling to reach the maximum capacity of fifteen. Calculate the cost to restock each spiral by multiplying the needed items by a price multiplier derived from the spiral sequence number. Identify empty spirals and add a priority restocking flag based on their position. Produce a loading manifest that lists the spiral number and the quantity to add. Return the total restocking cost and the manifest.

title: Sudoku Grid Row Validator
spec: Implement the validation using helper functions. The entry function `validate(rows)` receives a list of integer lists representing rows of a puzzle. Check each row for duplicates, ignoring zeros which represent empty spaces, and record the row number for any invalid row. Within each row, record the column index of any zero to build a list of missing cells. Find the first row that is completely filled and note its index. Generate a puzzle status report detailing the row number and whether it is complete or invalid. Return the status report and the invalid row numbers.

title: Crossword Puzzle Grid Populator
spec: Use a multi phase approach to populate the grid. The entry function `populate(words)` takes a list of strings representing answers to across clues. Calculate the required grid width by finding the longest word. Pad each word with spaces to match the grid width, tracking the clue number for each word. Identify intersecting letters by checking if the letter at a specific position matches the letter at the same position in the previous word. Produce a formatting log that pairs the clue number with the padded word. Return the padded words and the formatting log.

title: Word Game Multiplier Calculator
spec: Build the calculator using separate functions. The entry function `calculate(tiles)` accepts a list of integer base scores for played letter tiles. Apply a double letter score if the tile position in the word is a multiple of three. Apply a triple word score to the total if the final tile lands exactly on position seven. Calculate a running score tally at each tile placement. Identify high value tiles scoring more than five and note their placement position. Generate a turn summary listing the placement number and the cumulative score at that point. Return the final score and the summary log.

title: Miniature Golf Course Stroke Analyzer
spec: Structure the analysis with helper functions. The entry function `analyze(strokes)` takes a list of integers representing strokes taken per hole. Compare each score against a standard par of three, tracking the hole number starting from one. Calculate the cumulative score relative to par as the game progresses. Identify holes in one and record their hole number. Apply a penalty score cap of seven for any hole. Generate a scorecard string for each hole displaying the hole number, the strokes taken, and the relative par score. Return the final relative score and the scorecard.

title: Traffic Light Phase Simulator
spec: Model the junction cycle in distinct steps. The entry function `simulate(phases)` receives a list of integers representing the duration of green lights in seconds. Insert a three second yellow light and a two second red light after every green light, tracking the absolute phase number for all light changes. Identify long green phases exceeding sixty seconds and note their phase number to flag for pedestrian crossing priority. Calculate the total cycle time. Produce a timeline log pairing the phase number with the light color and duration. Return the total cycle time and the timeline log.

title: Printer Queue Optimizer
spec: Implement the queue optimization using helper functions. The entry function `optimize(jobs)` takes a list of integers representing page counts for print jobs. Separate the jobs into a fast track for jobs under ten pages and a bulk track for larger jobs, preserving the original submission number for each job. Calculate an estimated completion time by summing the pages of all preceding jobs in the sequence. Identify massive jobs over a hundred pages and insert a cooling period after them. Generate a print schedule detailing the submission number and the estimated completion time. Return the scheduled tracks and the print schedule.

title: Typography Kerning Adjuster
spec: Use multiple functions to adjust the spacing. The entry function `adjust(pairs)` receives a list of strings representing character pairs. Look up each pair in a standard spacing table to get the base distance, and reduce the spacing by two units if the pair contains a capital letter and a lowercase letter. Track the position index of each pair in the text line. Identify collision pairs where the adjusted spacing drops below zero and record their position. Create a typesetting log that pairs the position index with the final applied spacing. Return the total text width and the typesetting log.

title: Croquet Wicket Placement Analyzer
spec: Evaluate the layout of wickets on a croquet lawn. The entry function is `evaluate(wickets)` taking a list of integers for distances. Find cluster zones by collecting position indices where distance is zero, calculate difficulty momentum by multiplying each distance by its index, and detect long shots where distance exceeds ten at odd indices. Next, record positions of wickets with negative distances, find harmonic placements where distance equals its index, and format a text line for each combining its position and distance. Finally, calculate a turf wear metric by summing distances at prime indices, and find the position index of the longest distance. Execute all steps through helper functions, returning the total turf wear. An input of zero, five, twelve outputs the integer wear metric.

title: Tree Ring Growth Analyzer
spec: Analyze the annual growth rings of a tree. The entry function is `analyze(widths)` taking a list of integers representing ring widths. Construct moving sums by adding each width to its predecessor using its index, and find the earliest index where the width drops below five. Group widths into a dictionary by their index modulo three, compute the differences between each width and its position index, and format a botanical record string showing the index times ten alongside the width. Furthermore, verify if the widths strictly alternate by comparing neighbors via indices, sum the widths located at perfect square indices, and identify the last index where the width matches the very first ring. Organize the logic into helper procedures and return the sum of widths at perfect square indices. An input of five, twelve, fifty outputs this sum as an integer.

title: Tetherball Match Pendulum Tracker
spec: Process a sequence of pendulum swings in a tetherball match. The entry function is `evaluate(swings)` taking a list of integers representing arc degrees. Create a dictionary mapping the position index to the arc for arcs over twenty, determine the index of the first swing smaller than its predecessor, and generate strings formatting the word Swing, its index, and the arc. Calculate an interference score by summing absolute differences between adjacent swings using indices, keep arcs whose index divides sixty, and pair each arc with the one exactly three positions ahead. Finally, compute a velocity estimate by summing the product of arc and index for all even indices, and locate the position index of the lowest arc. Implement these evaluations through helper procedures that coordinate to return the velocity estimate. An input of ten, twenty, thirty returns this estimate integer.

title: Parachute Drop Zone Mapper
spec: Analyze target distances for a parachute landing exercise. The entry function is `analyze(distances)` passing a list of positive integers representing distances from the bullseye. Identify wind drift by keeping distances strictly greater than their position index, calculate an alternating drift sum by adding distances at even positions and subtracting at odd positions, and find the index of the first distance exceeding one hundred. Also, create tuples of each distance and its separation from the end of the sequence, verify symmetry by checking if distances match those at opposite ends via indices, and group distances into separate lists based on their index modulo three. Generate a textual log combining the zero-padded index and distance, and calculate a weighted average by summing the product of each distance and its index. Structure the logic into helpers, ultimately returning the weighted average. An input of twenty, fifty, twenty outputs this single integer.

title: Lighthouse Beam Timing Sequencer
spec: Calibrate the rotation timing of a lighthouse beam. The entry function is `calibrate(flashes)` with a list of integers for flash durations. First, generate tuples of position index and duration for flashes that are multiples of five, sum the durations at indices that are multiples of three, and find the index where a duration is exactly twice the preceding one. Next, create an HTML table string with columns for the index and duration, build a dictionary mapping the index to the duration modulo seven, and count flashes where the duration plus its index equals one hundred. Finally, find the first index containing a negative duration, and compute a peak efficiency score by finding the maximum product of any duration and its index. Divide these steps into helper routines that return the peak efficiency score. An input of ten, twenty outputs the score integer.

title: Scaffolding Structural Assessor
spec: Assess the weight distribution across scaffolding segments. The entry function is `assess(weights)` receiving a list of integers representing weight loads. Identify load spikes by finding indices of local maxima, compute a moving load by taking the difference between each weight and its predecessor, and build a lookup table mapping unique weights to their latest position index. Count how many segments have a weight equal to their index, format an HTML report mapping indices to list items, and find indices where the weight is a perfect square. Lastly, determine the maximum weight increase between adjacent segments using their indices, and calculate a stress score by summing the product of each weight and its index. Coordinate these calculations via helper routines and return the stress score. An input of four, nine, sixteen outputs the total stress integer.

title: Mechanical Watch Gear Train Evaluator
spec: Evaluate the gear ratios in a mechanical watch. The entry function is `evaluate(teeth)` processing a list of integers for tooth counts. Determine the index where the running total of teeth first exceeds one hundred, find the last index where the tooth count is strictly over fifty, and organize counts into a dictionary grouped by even or odd position indices. Generate a sequence of tuples pairing each index with double the tooth count, check for a symmetric layout by comparing tooth counts at opposite ends of the sequence, and calculate a kinetic score by summing the addition of each count and its index. Produce a schematic string separating the index and tooth count with a pipe, and locate positions where the tooth count is divisible by its non-zero index. Structure the implementation with helper functions, returning the kinetic score. An input of twelve, twenty outputs this score integer.

title: Seismograph Tremor Log Analyzer
spec: Analyze a log of seismic tremor magnitudes. The entry function is `analyze(tremors)` with a list of integer amplitudes. Find the index where the cumulative sum of tremors surpasses one thousand, identify duplicate amplitudes by recording their position indices, and extract sliding windows of three consecutive amplitudes using their indices. Build an interleaved sequence of indices and amplitudes, filter out amplitudes located at indices divisible by seven, and produce a list of strings joining the index and amplitude with a colon. Scale the readings by doubling amplitudes at even indices and tripling those at odd indices, and locate the position index of the absolute minimum amplitude recorded. Organize the logic into helper procedures and return the index of the minimum tremor. An input of five, ten, five returns this minimum index integer.

title: Brewery Bottling Line Monitor
spec: Monitor the pressure levels of bottles on a production line. The entry function is `monitor(pressures)` given a list of integers representing pressure readings. Create a mapping from each unique pressure to a list of its position indices, collect the indices of readings that fall below the overall average, and generate tuples of the index paired with the product of the pressure and its index. Filter out readings where the pressure equals the square of its position index, compile a comma-separated status string formatting the index in brackets followed by the pressure, and calculate a risk multiplier by multiplying pressures at prime indices. Count the bottles where the absolute difference between pressure and index is five, and find the index of the maximum pressure spike. Use small helper routines to execute the process and return the maximum pressure index. An input of thirty, forty outputs this integer index.

title: Choir Formation Arranger
spec: Arrange a choir based on the heights of the singers. The entry function is `arrange(heights)` working on a list of integer heights. Build a dictionary mapping each position index to the height, filter out singers whose height is lower than one hundred plus their index, and create name tag strings combining the index and height. Identify the position index of the tallest singer, assign singers to two different lists based on whether their index is even or odd, and generate a roster of tuples pairing the index with the height. Sum the heights of singers standing at prime position indices, and count how many singers have a height exactly equal to one hundred fifty plus their position index. Separate the process into helper routines and return the exact height match count. An input of one hundred sixty, one hundred seventy outputs this count integer.
